text:
What stronger breastplate than a heart untainted?
Thrice is he armed that hath his quarrel just,
And he but naked, though locked up in steel,
Whose conscience with injustice is corrupted.
plain: Nothing armors you like a clear conscience. A just cause makes you strong, and a corrupt one leaves you exposed.

text: So bad a death argues a monstrous life.
plain: The way someone dies shows how they lived.

text: Forbear to judge, for we are sinners all.
plain: Don't judge. Everyone has failed somewhere.
With you, a wilderness is full of people. Without you, the whole world is empty.

text:
If thou be’st Death, I’ll give thee England’s treasure,
Enough to purchase such another island,
So thou wilt let me live and feel no pain.
plain: Money can't buy off death, and a dying man would pay anything to live.

text: Small things make base men proud.
plain: Petty people puff up over petty wins.

text:
True nobility is exempt from fear;
More can I bear than you dare execute.
plain: Real nobility doesn't flinch. I can take more than you can dish out.

text: The first thing we do, let’s kill all the lawyers.
plain: A mob always starts by removing the people who understand the rules.

text: Some say the bee stings, but I say ’tis the bee’s wax; for I did but seal once to a thing, and I was never mine own man since.
plain: Be careful what you sign. One signature and you are never your own man again.

text: Trust nobody, for fear you be betrayed.
plain: Trust nobody, or you'll get betrayed.

text:
The trust I have is in mine innocence,
And therefore am I bold and resolute.
plain: Innocence gives you nerve. If you've done nothing wrong you can stand firm.

text:
And seeing ignorance is the curse of God,
Knowledge the wing wherewith we fly to heaven,
Unless you be possessed with devilish spirits,
You cannot but forbear to murder me.
plain: Ignorance is a curse, and knowledge is the wing we fly on.

text:
Great men have reaching hands; oft have I struck
Those that I never saw, and struck them dead.
plain: Powerful people reach farther than they can see. Their decisions land on strangers.

text:
Was never subject longed to be a king
As I do long and wish to be a subject.
plain: No subject ever wanted to be a king as much as I want to be a subject. The crown costs peace.

text:
Lord, who would live turmoiled in the court
And may enjoy such quiet walks as these?
This small inheritance my father left me
Contenteth me, and worth a monarchy.
plain: Why live in turmoil at court when a small, quiet life is worth a monarchy?

text:
I seek not to wax great by others’ waning,
Or gather wealth, I care not with what envy;
Sufficeth that I have maintains my state
And sends the poor well pleased from my gate.
plain: I don't want to rise by someone else's fall. What I have is enough, and I share it.

text: Let them obey that knows not how to rule.
plain: If you can't lead, follow.

text:
It is great sin to swear unto a sin,
But greater sin to keep a sinful oath.
plain: Breaking a bad promise is better than keeping it.

text:
Fear frames disorder, and disorder wounds
Where it should guard.
plain: Fear leads to disorder, and disorder hurts you right where you needed to be protected.

text:
And, father, do but think
How sweet a thing it is to wear a crown,
Within whose circuit is Elysium
And all that poets feign of bliss and joy.
plain: Think how sweet it is to wear the crown, with every bliss poets ever imagined inside it.

text: But thou prefer’st thy life before thine honour.
plain: You chose your life over your honour.

text:
Unless the adage must be verified,
That beggars mounted run their horse to death.
plain: Beggars on horseback ride the horse to death.

text:
The smallest worm will turn, being trodden on,
And doves will peck in safeguard of their brood.
plain: Even the smallest worm turns when trodden on.

text:
But, Clifford, tell me, didst thou never hear
That things ill got had ever bad success?
plain: Things gotten the wrong way never end well.

text:
I’ll leave my son my virtuous deeds behind,
And would my father had left me no more;
For all the rest is held at such a rate
As brings a thousand-fold more care to keep
Than in possession any jot of pleasure.
plain: I'd leave my son my good deeds and nothing more. All the rest costs more care to keep than it gives in pleasure.

text: Ill blows the wind that profits nobody.
plain: It's an ill wind that blows no one any good.

text:
Whiles lions war and battle for their dens,
Poor harmless lambs abide their enmity.
plain: When the strong fight for territory, the harmless pay for it.

text:
Gives not the hawthorn bush a sweeter shade
To shepherds looking on their silly sheep
Than doth a rich embroidered canopy
To kings that fear their subjects’ treachery?
plain: A hawthorn shade feels better to a shepherd than a canopy does to a king who fears his own people.

text:
So minutes, hours, days, months, and years,
Passed over to the end they were created,
Would bring white hairs unto a quiet grave.
plain: Minutes, hours, days, months and years pass, and a simple life ends at a quiet grave with white hair.

text:
Stay we no longer dreaming of renown,
But sound the trumpets and about our task.
plain: Stop dreaming of glory and get to the task.

text: Now my soul’s palace is become a prison.
plain: Your own mind can turn into the cell you can't leave.

text:
Let me embrace thee, sour adversity,
For wise men say it is the wisest course.
plain: Welcome adversity. Wise people say it is the wisest teacher.
My crown is in my heart, not on my head. It is called contentment, and kings rarely have it.
